claims: C1 the authority level of a section's rules is determined by the heading metadata (e.g., authority=user or authority=guideline)
C2 that authority level determines how those rules rank in conflicts with other instructions

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule that carries the user level of instruction authority, as assigned by its section heading's metadata
concepts.inference: the PROVIDES contract assigns this name and meaning; the source text's heading metadata (authority=user) instantiates it

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level H outranks level L in the instruction authority hierarchy root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this name and meaning; this node's text presupposes a ranking without stating it

concepts.name: section_authority
concepts.gloss: rule R is located under a section heading whose metadata assigns authority level L
concepts.inference: the source text's heading metadata (e.g., authority=user) is a fact about the document's structure; the relation between a rule and its heading's authority level is presupposed

concepts.name: outranks_in_conflict
concepts.gloss: rule R outranks rule S in a conflict between instructions
concepts.inference: the claim that authority level determines ranking in conflicts requires a relation between two rules and their relative precedence

ontology.gloss: R is a rule under a heading whose metadata assigns authority=user, so R carries user authority
R outranks S in a conflict when R carries user authority and S's section authority is a level below user
